subject: Search quality and cost next steps — hyperscaler comparisons & vector tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Post-call: search evaluation framing + next tests

Hi Anita / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

What we heard from Brightline:
- Primary goal: improve search relevance for customer support KB and reduce time-to-resolution.
- Key metrics: recall@5 (priority), MRR, and retrieval latency (95th pctile) under concurrent query load.
- Cost sensitivity: want a rough estimate of per-million-query inference cost and vector storage/embedding compute cost.

What Redwood can bring to the comparison:
- Baseline tests vs hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) + an Anthropic-style API if you want. We can run identical embed+retrieve+rerank pipelines and surface recall@k, latency distributions, and unit economics.
- Reranking: we recommend a small reranker model for quality lift (quantized 8-bit) and compare with reranking done at the hyperscaler endpoints.
- Vector dims to test: 128 / 256 / 512. We’ll include cost delta and expected recall lift per dimension.

Proposed next tests (please confirm):
1) Controlled batch: 10k sample queries derived from your support logs (you can share CSV). Run embed->ANN retrieve->rerank across three providers. Capture recall@1/5/10 and p95 latency at 100 qps.
2) Vector dim sweep: 128/256/512 for Redwood model + same dims using AWS/GCP embeddings where possible.
3) Cost model: include token/embedding per-call cost, vector store monthly storage per 1M vectors, and per-query compute for rerank.
4) Edge-case check: long-context queries (seq length 1024) to measure latency variance and KV-cache behavior.

Attachments: mutual action plan draft (mutual-action-plan.pdf) and a short CSV template for sample queries.

Next steps: if that plan looks right, share a 10k sample CSV (anonymized) and we’ll schedule the first comparative run next week.

Thanks —
Logan

Logan — thanks for the forward. High-level runbook and test details below (we should drop this into the GDrive link after review).

1) Config matrix (Redwood baseline):
- Embedding models: rwd-embed-small (128d), rwd-embed-medium (256d), rwd-embed-large (512d)
- ANN index: HNSW (efConstruction=200, M=32) with Faiss on NVMe nodes (replicated)
- Reranker: rwd-rank-lite (quantized 8-bit), fallback rwd-rank-base (fp16)
- Serving settings: batching target 32, max latency target 200ms; autoscale to maintain 100 qps.

2) Metrics & measurement:
- Recall@1/5/10 and MRR computed on the 10k labeled sample (we’ll ask Brightline to mark ground-truth doc IDs for the sample).
- Latency: sample end-to-end 95th and 99th percentiles at 100 qps sustained for 30 minutes. Use realistic arrival jitter.
- Cost model: report (a) embedding compute cost per 1M texts, (b) vector store monthly storage per 1M vectors (assume 16 bytes per dim + metadata), (c) rerank compute cost per 1M reranks. We’ll provide a spreadsheet with numbers.

3) Hyperscaler parity tests:
- For AWS/GCP we’ll request equivalent embedding dims where available and run the same ANN+rerank pipeline. Note: cloud vendors often charge higher per-call embedding costs and have different latency profiles for small reranker models. We should align tokenization/embedding semantics to be comparable.

4) Quick cost back-of-envelope (very rough):
- Embedding compute: Redwood (rwd-embed-medium/256d) ~ $40–$70 per 1M texts (depends on batching).
- Vector storage: ~ $8–$12 per month per 1M vectors (512d higher end).
- Rerank compute: ~ $100–$180 per 1M reranks for small fp16 model; quantized path can cut this by ~40%.
- Retrieval-only (no rerank) per-million-query inference cost: ~ $60–$90. Retrieval + rerank: ~ $160–$270 per 1M queries.

Caveats: numbers depend on batching, disk choices (NVMe vs S3-backed), and replication factor. In hyperscalers we often see embedding per-call costs 1.5–2x higher; network egress and request overheads can push p95 latency up.

5) Deliverables & schedule:
- Day 0 (receive 10k sample): sanity check + ground-truth mapping (1 business day).
- Day 1–2: run Redwood baseline across dims + collect metrics.
- Day 3–4: run hyperscaler baselines (coord with Samir if Atlas is running theirs).
- Day 5: consolidated report + cost spreadsheet + recommended config for production (includes batching + quantization knobs).

Attachments: latency comparison diagram and a template cost sheet.

If that looks good I can populate the Drive folder and start the runs as soon as they drop the CSV.

—Sergio
